children: The artificial intelligence investment boom is expected to remain an important support for corporate earnings through at least 2027, with Goldman Sachs saying an outright decline in AI spending is unlikely before 2028 or later.
Goldman Chief Economist Jan Hatzius said S&P 500
earnings per share are on track to grow 36% in 2026, helped by gains on private investment stakes and a windfall from AI investment, including margin expansion at semiconductor

Goldman does expect that extraordinary pace to cool. Goldman’s U.S. equity strategists see S&P 500 EPS growth slowing to 11% in 2027 as gains from private investments fade and AI spending moves closer to a peak. But Hatzius said the slowdown could be much sharper only if AI investment begins to decline outright, a scenario Goldman views as unlikely until 2028 or beyond.
Goldman argues that talk of an earnings bubble is overblown, even as companies are currently “over-earning” relative to a more normal cycle because of the AI-driven boost.

AI infrastructure is estimated to contribute roughly 15 percentage points to S&P 500 EPS growth in 2026, followed by 11 points in 2027 and 8 points in 2028. Hyperscalers add another 4, 3 and 3 percentage points, respectively.

title: AI investment boom unlikely to fade before 2028 - Goldman
